newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa still firmer, Sept falters at 1,150.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa still firmer, Sept falters at 1,150.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures were firmer by the close on Friday but values were off their best and benchmark September again faltered at the key 1,150 stg barrier, the peak seen for three days in a row.
Cargill was seen as a buyer in the morning, lifting the second-month contract to the day's high of 1,150 stg, the peak seen since Wednesday, traders said.
The run-up was stalled again at 1,150 and the buying soon stopped. It finished at 1,145 stg, still nine stg higher on the day. Its intraday low was 1,133.
"The charts are still bullish but the market has to clear the triple top at 1,150 before moving much higher," said one.
The next layer of resistance is seen at Tuesday's peak of 1,162, followed by the June 1996 high of 1,172, based on second-month continuation chart.
But the downside is safe as long as September holds above 1,100.
Overall volume at 4,637 lots was far from impressive. Switches were again the main contributor, with Sept/Dec spread trading at around level money.
The September cocoa had gained a sharp 15 percent this month alone on the back of keen fund, spec and manufacturer buying.
One trade house estimated the funds and the specs were probably 18,000 lots long in London and 32,000 lots longs in New York.
The funds might renew their buying at above 1,172 and this would pave the way for a challenge at 1,200.
The second quarter European grind data, due next week, are expected to be mixed, traders said.

On the supply front, the market will start seeing the arrivals of mid-crop cocoa from Ivory Coast and Nigeria from next week. Although the crops are slightly delayed, the quality is said to be good. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
